subject: How does lavaan use data in cross-lagged paths

messages.author: 60b9b3430407b48b
messages.subject: How does lavaan use data in cross-lagged paths
parts:
Dear All,
I would appreciate it if you helped me regarding the following topic. Your answers will help me a lot in solving an issue in my thesis.

I used Lavaan for doing the following autoregressive cross-lagged model. the data for Esdq is available from 3years to 17 years old children at baseline with an index of 0
Esdq1: 6 -17 years age rangeEsdq2: 11-17 years age rangePA0:  0-17 yearsPA1: 6-17 years PA2:11-17 years 
I want to find out how lavaan (R) uses the data for cross-lagged paths. Does it only use paired data from the previous time-point to the next time-point ? or does it use the data from the previous time-point that there is no pair data for it at the next time-point. In other words: does lavaan use only data of participants that they have valid data at two-time points in terms of cross-lagged paths or not?
ReciprocalcovModel3 <-
  '
  Esdq2 ~ Esdq1+Esdq0+ PA1+Bmi2
  Esdq1 ~ Esdq0+ PA0+Ebmi1
  PA2 ~ PA1+ PA0+Esdq1+Bmi2
  PA1 ~ PA0+Esdq0+Ebmi1
  Esdq0~UBmi0+SESc0
  PA0~UBmi0+SESc0
  Esdq0 ~~ PA0
  Esdq1 ~~ PA1
  Esdq2 ~~ PA2

 '                        
ReciprocalcovModel3.fit<- sem(ReciprocalcovModel3,data = X8J21,se = "robust", fixed.x =FALSE, conditional.x = FALSE,missing="pairwise",group = "Sex0", ordered=c("PA0","PA1","PA2"))

summary(ReciprocalcovModel3.fit, fit.measures = TRUE,standardized = TRUE,ci = TRUE,   rsquare = TRUE)

Best regards,
Parisa
